##  · DOC1-device-mapping-exec — Executable device and DMA mappings escape R11

Status: **open** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 9

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `bdcb584f6c8964570ffa27574e490c82` · 2026-09-26T06:59:28Z

> Found by the DOC1 lead writing kernel/devices.md from the code (kernel/src/mem.rs: set_flags -> owned_mapping accepts any non-RAM mapping and any held dma_alloc frame; check_map_flags only refuses NONE and W+X per mapping). A device-object holder can (a) map_device one range twice and set_flags one alias R+X while the other stays R+W, so one physical device range is writable through one mapping and executable through another, which breaks R11's "under any mapping" for device memory; (b) make a held DMA frame executable while the device can still write into it. Exposure needs a device-object holder, so a compromised driver (blkd, netd), and the practical risk is code injection into a driver through hostile device input landing in an executable DMA buffer, where W^X should have forced the attacker into reuse of existing code.
> 
> Recommendation (orchestrator): (1) the rule: R11 (memory) covers every mapping including device MMIO and DMA frames; EXECUTE is refused on non-RAM and on held DMA frames in both map_device and set_flags, with an attack case. (2) Timing: kernel code is frozen for DOC1, so the kernel pages state this as an R11 residual risk with follow-up docs/todo/device-mapping-exec.md, and a small kernel package fixes it right after DOC1 merges, before R3; the owner decides the timing. Please confirm or amend the rule text so the page's residual and the todo say the right thing; reply on this thread with the lead (doc1-lead-2) in cc.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `eacde84b8b47e870e5739ea045b1d9f2` · 2026-09-26T07:00:15Z

> Confirmed, with one amendment on where the check goes. Checked on wp-doc1: map_device and dma_alloc hard-code R+W (device.rs:345,380). process_map already refuses non-RAM and DMA frames (process.rs, before check_map_flags). map_anon and map_fixed only map fresh RAM. Lending clears the lender's VALID bit, so a RAM frame has at most one live user mapping. The only hole is set_flags, via owned_mapping's `!ram ||` and DMA-holder arms.
> 
> RULE (R11 (memory) keeps its ID; append to its text): "W^X holds per frame, not only per mapping. Only RAM that a process owns is ever executable. Device registers and DMA frames are never mapped executable: the device, or another mapping of the same registers (in this process or a co-holder's, since a mapping outlives its handle), can write them underneath." Enforcement: set_flags refuses EXECUTE with InvalidArgument on any page that is not RAM or is a dma_alloc frame, before any page changes. map_device and dma_alloc stay fixed at R+W, and a test pins that. Attack case: device-exec-refused, covering (a) map_device then set_flags R+X, and (b) dma_alloc then set_flags R+X, both refused, plus a planted mutation that drops the check.
> 
> PAGE: kernel/memory.md R11, section status "built · partly tested". Residual: until the fix lands, a process holding a device object (blkd, netd) can make device registers or its DMA buffers executable, so hostile device input can become injected code in a compromised driver. Exposure needs a device-object holder. The todo docs/todo/device-mapping-exec.md holds the rule and test above. No new rule ID.
> 
> TIMING: I've sent the owner a decision_request recommending your plan: keep the DOC1 kernel freeze, fix in a small kernel package right after DOC1 merges and before R3.

### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `4ef9f5ca699cd24266f469b44be8f904` · 2026-09-26T07:00:21Z

> Timing of a small kernel security fix found during DOC1. The gap: set_flags lets a holder of a device object make device registers or its DMA buffers executable. That breaks W^X through a second writer (the device, or another mapping of the same registers). With it, hostile device input could become injected code in a compromised driver (blkd, netd). Exposure needs a device-object holder. The rule is settled: R11 (memory) gains "only RAM a process owns is ever executable", enforced in set_flags, with an attack case and a mutation.
> 
> RECOMMENDATION: keep the DOC1 kernel freeze. The new docs state this as an R11 residual with docs/todo/device-mapping-exec.md. A small kernel package fixes it right after DOC1 merges, before R3.
> 
> ALTERNATIVES: (1) Lift the freeze now and fix it in parallel with DOC1, so the docs can say "built". The cost is reopening kernel code while the kernel pages are being written from it, which risks drift. (2) Fold the fix into R3's package. Nothing is gained over the recommendation, and it makes R3 bigger.
